certainty.note: Colonial frontiers are approximate: a scatter of coastal settlements, plantation districts and trading posts, with the interior lines of North America, the Hudson Bay shore, Australia's interior and the Canadian north undrawn by treaty. Sharp exceptions: the Mississippi line of 1763 (Treaty of Paris, Article VII: 'a line drawn along the middle of the River Mississippi') and the Great Lakes and 31st-parallel boundary of 1783; small islands and city enclaves (Gibraltar, Minorca, Hong Kong Island) are exact.

Dominion, colony and treaty-port borders are fixed by statute or treaty (Labrador by the 11 March 1927 decision, CAN). Exceptions: the occupation zones of 1914-1922 (Khuzestan) and 1941-1946 (southern Iran, IRN), and the protected states of the Gulf and Aden hinterland, are soft.

sources.note: British privateers took Essequibo and Demerara on 24 February 1781; the French held it from 27 February 1782 (body) or 22 January 1782 (infobox) to 1783; 'In 1796 it was permanently occupied by the British'; returned 1802-1803; British again after 1803; 13 August 1814 cession.

sources.title: Berbice
sources.note: Occupied 27 February 1781; 'In January 1782, the colonies were recaptured by the French'; restored to the Dutch by the Treaty of Paris of 1783; captured 22 April 1796; restored to the Batavian Republic 27 March 1802; reoccupied September 1803; ceded 1814.

sources.title: Acadia
sources.note: 'Acadia was conquered in 1710 during Queen Anne's War'; 'confirmed by the Treaty of Utrecht of 1713'; Île Saint-Jean and Île Royale stayed French.

sources.title: Île-Royale
sources.note: Louisbourg fell 26 July 1758; infobox 'Under British military occupation (1758–1763)'; 'ceded to the British Empire after the Seven Years' War'. Does not name the 1763 treaty for the island.

sources.title: French and Indian War
sources.note: Fort Beauséjour June 1755; Quebec September 1759; Articles of Capitulation of Montreal on 8 September (1760); Treaty of Paris 10 February 1763 with the cession of Canada.

sources.title: Northwest Indian War
sources.note: 'Fort Lernoult and Fort Miami were abandoned by the British in 1796 as a condition of the Jay Treaty'; year only.

sources.title: Treaty of 1818
sources.note: Signed 20 October 1818; ratifications exchanged 30 January 1819; Article II fixes the 49th parallel to the Stony Mountains; land north of 49N ceded to the UK, land south of it (Red River) to the United States.

sources.title: Territorial evolution of the United States
sources.note: Webster–Ashburton Treaty 13 October 1842 ('defined the border with the United Kingdom east of the Rocky Mountains'); Treaty of 1818 convention dated 30 January 1819; Oregon Treaty dated 17 July 1846.

sources.title: Mosquito Coast
sources.note: Infobox 'Protectorate of England (1638–1707)' and 'Protectorate of Great Britain (1707–1787)'; 1786 Convention of London (evacuation); recognition as independent in 1837; 'a new protectorate' in 1844. Does not say the protectorate ended.

sources.title: First Anglo-Burmese War
sources.note: Invasion of Arakan 1 February 1825, Mrauk-U defeated 1 April; Treaty of Yandabo 24 February 1826 cedes Assam, Arakan and the Tenasserim coast south of the Salween. Silent on Martaban.

sources.title: British Overseas Territories
sources.note: fx-44 R146: 'Before 1 January 1983, the territories were officially referred to as the Crown Colonies'; 'renamed British Dependent Territories'; 'In 2002, the British Parliament passed the British Overseas Territories Act 2002' which 'introduced the current name'. Gives no royal assent date.

notes:
WHAT THE ROW IS. Cliopatria's 'British Colonial Empire' (1706-1999, 90 shapes, max 13.69 M km2 in 1900) is an aggregate of British possessions drawn as effective control in coarse grid cells: the Thirteen Colonies, Newfoundland, Nova Scotia and Hudson Bay, the Caribbean, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Africa outside the british-africa and british-gold-coast rows, then the remnants. It is NOT the whole British Empire: the Indian subcontinent is drawn by british-empire (1757-1858) and british-raj (1859-1947), Aden is in no Cliopatria shape, and what a shape draws is not always what a page says. Type is 'colony' because the territory is a dependency of the metropole (kingdom-of-great-britain, then united-kingdom).

Q8680 SHARED WITH british-empire. Both rows carry Wikidata Q8680 and Wikipedia 'British Empire'. They are different states in Cliopatria's drawing (this global aggregate 1706-1999 versus the East India Company's India 1757-1858) and are NOT merged: british-empire is the counterpart named by many Indian dossiers (gwalior-state, nawab-of-awadh, kingdom-of-mysore and others) and has its own dossier from sa-06-c. The 'British Empire' article draws no line between the two.

START AND END. identity.start is 1704 (TE: 'Gibraltar | 1704 | Captured by Britain'), two years before the first Cliopatria shape (new keyframe british-colonial-empire_1704 covers 1704-1705). BE gives no establishment date for the empire. The end is 1999, the last Cliopatria year; BE puts the symbolic end at the Hong Kong handover of 1 July 1997 (new keyframe _1997 drops Hong Kong). The remnants continue as british-overseas-territories (2000-).

INFOBOX AREA. BE: 'by 1920 it covered 35.5 million km2'. This row's 1920 shape is 12.03 M km2; the six British-family rows alive in 1920 (this row 12.03, british-africa 10.07, commonwealth-of-australia 7.78, british-raj 4.94, british-gold-coast 1.20, kingdom-of-great-britain 0.77) sum to 36.77 M km2, 3.6 percent above the infobox. The Cliopatria row's maximum (13.69 M km2, 1900) is thus not the empire's area; no keyframe was widened to reach 35.5 M km2.

OVERLAPS. (1) english-colonial-empire (1609-1779) covers 1709-1712 as well; 771 of its 777 cells in 1709 are this row's cells, and this dossier treats 1709 as a hand-over of rows (ledger 1709, confidence 1). (2) Canada: the Cliopatria shape keeps the Dominion's land in this row until 1928, while canada.json (state from 1 July 1867) lists this dossier as its predecessor and asks for a vassal link. The verdicts for 1868 to 1928 therefore remove the Dominion's provinces from the direct shape in step with the CAN transfers (four founding provinces 1868; Rupert's Land and the North-Western Territory 1870; British Columbia 1871; everything but Newfoundland and Labrador from 1873), and the ledger carries Canada as a vassal from 1867 to 11 December 1931 (SW). Newfoundland and Labrador (a separate colony; Labrador to Newfoundland on 11 March 1927, CAN) stay direct land. New Zealand is treated the same way (verdicts 1908-1947 remove it; vassal 1907 to November 1947) and Australia (vassal 1901 to 1942). (3) commonwealth-of-australia (Cliopatria 1905-) starts four years after federation; Cliopatria keeps Australia whole in this row through 1904, so new keyframe _1901 removes it and the Dominion lands from 1901. (4) Sub-colony dossiers (british-honduras, belize, guyana, jamaica, barbados and others) describe ground this row also draws: the same land at a finer scale, not rivals.

EFFECTIVE CONTROL VERSUS CLAIMS. Cliopatria draws effective control, so the interior claims (Western Australia, South Australia and the Northern Territory before settlement; New Zealand's South Island in 1840; the Canadian north) are drawn only to the extent the cells go. The keyframe corrections follow the shape and say where a page contradicts it; they do not paint nominal claims. Where a page lists a territory that no cell draws, it is a gap (see below), not a correction; where a page contradicts a cell the verdict says so.

BOOKKEEPING MOVES (confidence 1, no page). 1757: the three Indian cells pass to british-empire. 1794: Cliopatria's shape drops Gibraltar, which the kingdom-of-great-britain row draws. 1914: Zanzibar's cells go to british-africa. 1946: Iraq (5 to 1,649 cells), Jordan, Israel, Palestine, Kuwait, Saudi and Syrian cells appear in the 1946 shape; TE has Palestine as a mandate 1920-1948 but no 1946 Iraq entry. Repair 2026-10-31: the 1946 keyframe now removes them and the three events that treated them as a row hand-over are deleted.

GIBRALTAR AND MINORCA. TE dates Gibraltar 1704 and Menorca 1708 (occupied), 1713 (ceded), 1756 (French occupation), 1798-1802 (British). The shapes keep Minorca British until 1780 (corrected in the 1757 and 1762 verdicts) and drop it in 1781; the ledger follows TE. The Anglo-Spanish peace is '13 July' on the UT page with no year; the ledger puts Spain's cession in July 1713 at confidence 2.

YEMEN AND STRAY CELLS. The 1870 shape adds Yemen (1,381 cells), Oman (21) and Saudi Arabia (18) cells which no page supports (ADEN dates Aden from January 1839 and its first interior treaty from 1886, and is silent on 1870-1889); the 1870-1885 verdicts remove them and the Aden vassal events (1886-1967) carry the protectorate. Single stray cells (Cote d'Ivoire 1727-1743, Thailand from 1825, Afghanistan from 1840, Venezuela from 1877, Brazil, Uruguay 1807-1808) rest on no page read; they are named in the shape verdicts and left in the shape as 'unverified'.

BRIDGING EVENTS (confidence 1). The ledger lists the shapes' own frontier growth where no page dates it, so that every shape change has an event: 1718 and 1752 (the Carolinas and Virginia), 1721 (the interior of Newfoundland, Quebec and Ontario), 1734 and 1744 (the Mosquito shore), 1772 (westward growth), 1822 (Hudson's Bay Company posts), 1846 (60 Indian cells), 1848 (the far north-west). None rests on a page; the only page-dated settlement is Georgia (TE, 1732, confidence 2). The Mosquito Coast protectorate (TE: 1668-1861) is a vassal pair 1704 to 1861 at the shore's widest (Cliopatria's 1846 cells). The Oregon division of 1846 (TE) is the one dated loss of that decade.

GAPS (territories TE lists that no shape draws, so no ledger event): Gold Coast 1788-1872 (Cliopatria drops its Gold Coast cells in 1788; TE has the colony from 1874 and the british-gold-coast row starts in 1873); Aden (TE: Bombay Presidency 1839, separate Crown colony 1937, Federation of South Arabia 1963); Malta (TE 1800-1964), the Ionian Islands (1815-1864), Heligoland (1814-1890), Cyprus (annexed 1914, independent 1960), Seychelles (1814-1976), Ascension (1815-) and Tristan da Cunha (1816-); the Straits Settlements (TE 1826-1946) beyond the 4 to 8 Malaysia cells the shapes draw; Manila 1762 (P63: taken in the war, restored in 1763; not drawn). Each is a few cells at most.

VERDICT SCOPE. 44 of the 90 shapes are 'adjust' (cell-level country and admin1 diffs checked against pages read); 46 are 'ok'. 13 of the 14 pages allowed were opened: TE six times with different questions (its tables are long and the reading model would not give them verbatim in one pass), BE, UT, P63, P83, AM, AD, CAN, AUS, MES, IRN, ADEN and SW. Verdicts that rest on no dated page say 'unverified: page budget'.

(c) Guadeloupe: no shape draws it (0 cells), so it has no event although the 1810 and 1814 pages date it. (d) Cliopatria's cells lag the pages (Senegal 1762 against 1758, Guyana 1797 against 1796, Réunion to 1819 against 1814); the events carry the page dates and the notes say by how much the shape differs. (e) The Peace of Paris (1783) page gives Dominica and Saint Vincent in the preliminary articles of 20 January 1783; TE has Dominica a colony again only in 1784.
